citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Acquisition and disposition records documented that a total of 11 sugar gliders acquired from 2 separate instances of
international import (one on 06/04/2026 and the other on 08/26/2026) were found weak upon arrival and died within 24 to
48 hours. The records indicated that the animals were “separated and given emergency care” once identified. A facility
representative explained the care provided as giving fluids orally to the animals and giving them time/space to recover. A
veterinarian was not consulted for the care of these animals in critical/emergent condition, nor did the attending
veterinarian approve of this mode of treatment for these specific circumstances. The attending veterinarian further
explained not knowing that the licensee imported sugar gliders internationally and expressed concerns over the medical
implications in terms of acquiring potentially compromised animals or disease carriers that may require a specific care
plan that was not yet discussed. Without veterinary consultation, care given to these animals especially those in critical
condition is inadequate and may have resulted in pain, distress and death of these sugar gliders. The licensee must
develop a mechanism of direct and frequent communication with the veterinarian so that timely and accurate information
on problems of animal health, behavior and well-being is conveyed in a timely fashion and treated adequately. Correct by
11/04/2026.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “B” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by December 16, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by October 30, 2026.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
